analysis.title: Equity Thematic Strategy: Midterm Elections, Scenario Analysis, Baskets
key_insights: US midterms are a little over a month away. Betting odds (Kalshi/Polymarket midpoint) give Democrats 92% for the House and 63% for the Senate. The generic ballot favors Democrats by about 8.3 points (RCP), versus about 2 points in 2024 and about 1 point in 2022 at the same point in the year.

JPM expects the equity impact of the midterms to be more nuanced than in the 2024 presidential election and to favor stock picking over sector bets. The report identifies 125+ companies across three scenario baskets: Gridlock, Blue Wave and Red Wall.

Six-month basket performance has favored Gridlock (+9%) and Blue Wave (+1%) over Red Wall (-1.5%). A separate Agnostic basket covers names expected to benefit in all three outcomes, and a Government Spending basket covers federal-spending exposure.

JPM expects AI capex momentum to stay intact after the midterms and possibly strengthen in 2027 and 2028. No comprehensive AI regulatory bill looks likely near term, and states continue to lead on datacenter restrictions.

Gridlock would help mainly by limiting downside policy risk. Beneficiaries are Healthcare (less Medicaid cuts and federal drug-pricing legislation), Defense and already-appropriated infrastructure, and select Technology names (lower odds of new antitrust, AI and privacy legislation).

Blue Wave beneficiaries are hospitals (if OBBBA Medicaid cuts are delayed or reversed), Medicaid managed care, municipal water and environmental services, renewable-exposed utilities, and some application software as relatively defensive exposure. Veto power and the filibuster would limit how much Democratic legislation becomes law.

Red Wall would be the most supportive backdrop for the AI/infrastructure buildout. Beneficiaries are datacenter and power names, electrical equipment, energy services, E&C, building materials, traditional energy and nuclear, railroads, financials (regional banks especially, via capital-rule relief), defense, cybersecurity and Medicare Advantage insurers.

Markets have had to weigh a Blue Sweep against the consensus Gridlock case over the past 1-2 months. Historical base rate: the sitting president's party has lost about 27 House seats and about 3 Senate seats on average over 23 midterms since 1934. The current Senate is 53 Republican and the House majority is 218.

S&P 500 returns since 1950 have been better under gridlock: +21% vs +18% for single-party control by election date, and +25% vs +18% by the date the new Congress starts. Upside may be limited by the strong setup: S&P 500 is up about 60% in the presidential term (average full term about 39%) and Nasdaq 100 is up about 75%.

2026 drawdowns are unusually shallow for a midterm year. The S&P 500 max drawdown is -9.1% YTD, about half the usual midterm decline. The Russell 2000 drawdown is -11.2% YTD, the lowest small-cap midterm-year drawdown since 1990.

Sector pattern around elections (since 1990): Semis (+7.2% cumulative from 1M before to 1M after), Software (+4.2%) and Tech Hardware (+3.7%) outperform across the full window. A buy-the-dip-then-rally pattern appears in Consumer Durables, Consumer Discretionary Retail, Media, Materials, Transportation, Health Care Equipment and Utilities. Telecom Services and Household & Personal Products tend to rally then dip.

The S&P 500 options market prices only a modest election event premium, with no pronounced kink in the term structure. Historically VIX rises into midterms, peaks about one month before election day and resets lower afterward. The VIX curve sits well below levels seen before prior midterms, and JPM favors positioning for a higher VIX ahead of the event.

Other macro risks cited alongside the election: rates, Iran/oil and AI disruption. The report also shows gasoline at $4.48 and diesel at $6.47 per gallon, and federal debt held by the public at 98.7% of GDP (total debt 122.6%).

Republicans may use the lame-duck session for a mini budget reconciliation bill. It could be sized at $3-500B with defense and farmer support, which would be a net positive for Defense (JPRAEROD) and the Low-end Consumer (JPRLOWCO) baskets.

Long-end rates could be affected by the outcome. JPM expects Gridlock or Blue Wave to be marginally more favorable than Red Wall. Fed funds futures currently price about +4.8 25bp hikes net for 2026, versus +7.8 for the midterm-year average, per Figure 11 as printed.
Historical S&P 500 performance after midterm elections is positive: the average gain is +1.3% at 1M, +7.1% at 3M, +13.4% at 6M and +14.6% at 12M, and the 12M median is +13.6%.

S&P 500 2026 consensus: sales +12.3%, net income +32.8%, margin 16.2%. The Magnificent 7 net income grows +55.4% and the JPM AI 30 basket +59.6%. Gridlock basket net income +63.2% in 2026 but -3% in 2027. Red Wall basket +50.6% in 2026 and -7% in 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Screens favorably under Gridlock and Blue Wave. Policy visibility could improve risk/reward for large-cap pharma, health IT and SMid biotech.

Bipartisan munitions replenishment, multi-year defense programs and already-appropriated infrastructure spending support the group in Gridlock. Higher defense spending in Red Wall and a possible lame-duck reconciliation bill add to it.
Semis, Software and Tech Hardware have outperformed across the full window around midterms since 1990. Gridlock lowers the odds of new antitrust, AI and privacy legislation.
Would gain from lighter supervision and capital-rule relief in a Red Wall, with regional banks most leveraged. Financials have historically de-rated into midterms and stayed flat afterward.
Traditional energy and nuclear would benefit from a Red Wall. Energy has historically peaked just before midterms and lagged after (-3.2% at 1M after, -4.3% at 6M after).
Renewable-exposed utilities would benefit in a Blue Wave. Utilities have historically held up into midterms and then faded.
Pre-election strength has historically reversed after the election, with Household & Personal Products and Food/Bev/Tobacco lagging.
Historical pattern of a pre-election dip followed by a post-election rally (Durables & Apparel -0.6% before, +2.9% after; Retail -2.0% before, +1.5% after). A tactical buy-the-dip setup.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 2026 consensus (I/B/E/S): sales $19,825B (+12.3% y/y) and net income $3,217B (+32.8% y/y), with net margin rising from 13.7% to 16.2%. The 2026 forward P/E is 21.6x.
Magnificent 7 consensus: 2026 net income $966B (+55.4% y/y, 43% of S&P 500 growth contribution). S&P 500 ex-Mag 7 net income +25.0%. The JPM AI 30 basket net income is +59.6% in 2026.

Basket aggregates, 2027 net income growth (consensus): S&P 500 +14.1%, Gridlock -3%, Blue Wave +5%, Red Wall -7%, Agnostic 0%, Government Spending +14%. 2026 growth: Gridlock +63.2%, Red Wall +50.6%, Blue Wave +20.2%.
By sector, consensus 2026 net income growth is led by Energy (+89.9%), Communication Services (+60.5%) and Information Technology (+52.2%). Health Care is +1.2%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Large Democratic lead, up from about 2 points in 2024 and about 1 point in 2022 at the same time of year. It raises the odds of a divided or Democratic Congress.
Kalshi/Polymarket midpoint. A Democratic House is close to the market's base case.
Senate odds have strengthened noticeably in the past 1-2 months, raising Blue Sweep risk against the consensus Gridlock case.
Fed expectations have moved higher in 2026. Rates are listed as one of the macro concerns around the election.
High fuel prices weigh on the consumer.

trade_ideas.description: Position for a higher VIX ahead of the US midterm elections
trade_ideas.rationale: VIX has historically risen into midterms and peaked about one month before election day, while the current curve prices limited election risk.
trade_ideas.risk: VIX resets lower after the election, and the options market currently prices little event premium.

trade_ideas.description: Buy the typical pre-election dip and position for a post-election rally in Consumer Durables & Apparel, Consumer Discretionary Retail, Media & Entertainment and Materials
trade_ideas.rationale: These groups historically fall in the month before the election and rally in the month after.
trade_ideas.risk: Sector hit rates are mixed since 1990, with no perfect hit rates.

trade_ideas.description: Hold Semis, Software and Tech Hardware through the full window from 1M before to 1M after the election
trade_ideas.rationale: They have outperformed across the full window, led by Semis (+7.2% cumulative).
trade_ideas.risk: Midterm sector performance has been mixed, and the S&P 500 is already up about 60% in the presidential term.

trade_ideas.description: Avoid Telecommunication Services and Household & Personal Products into the post-election window
trade_ideas.rationale: They show a rally-then-dip pattern (Telecom +1.1% before, -2.4% after; Household & Personal Products +1.6% before, -0.2% after).
trade_ideas.risk: Small average moves and mixed hit rates.

trade_ideas.description: Own the AI Agnostic basket (JPRAG26M) for outcome-independent exposure to advertising revenues and lower policy uncertainty
trade_ideas.rationale: Names in it are expected to benefit under Gridlock, Blue Wave and Red Wall.

risk_factors: Blue Sweep versus consensus Gridlock: Democratic odds have risen in the past 1-2 months, and AI/datacenter-regulation-exposed names carry more risk in that case.
Macro risks that could intensify before the election: rates, Iran/oil and AI disruption.
Executive action and agency enforcement remain live risks for healthcare, tech antitrust and AI even under gridlock.
The strong setup into the midterms (S&P 500 up about 60% in the presidential term, ahead of the average full-term gain of about 39%) may limit further upside.
Consumer pressure from gasoline at $4.48 and diesel at $6.47 per gallon.
Fiscal risk: federal debt held by the public is 98.7% of GDP, and must-pass budget and debt-ceiling fights loom.
Long-end rate sensitivity to the election outcome, with Red Wall seen as marginally less favorable.
Midterm sector hit rates are mixed with no perfect hit rates, so sector bets are less reliable than in a presidential cycle.

tension_points.bull_case: Gridlock has historically been positive for equities: S&P 500 +21% vs +18% under single-party control (+25% vs +18% from the start of the new Congress). Gridlock and Blue Wave baskets have outperformed Red Wall over 6 months, and a split Congress limits downside policy risk.
tension_points.bear_case: The S&P 500 is already up about 60% in the presidential term, so some upside may be limited. A Blue Sweep, which markets have weighed more in the past 1-2 months, would raise regulatory risk for AI/datacenter-exposed names and favor Red Wall-sensitive deregulation and buildout names less.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Democrats taking both chambers (Senate odds at 63% and rising) would test the consensus Gridlock case.

tension_points.bull_case: VIX has historically risen into midterms and peaked about one month before election day, and the curve now prices limited election risk, so long-VIX positioning has room to pay.
tension_points.bear_case: The options market shows no pronounced kink and the VIX curve sits well below prior midterm levels, so a calm tape (2026 drawdowns are shallow) can keep implied vol low.
tension_points.what_invalidates: VIX peaking about one month before election day and then resetting lower would end the long-vol setup.
